subject: Accounting
title: Estate and Inheritance Tax
description: A fast breakdown of Estate and Inheritance Tax for builders.

hook.text: When a billionaire dies, the government can tax up to 40% of their estate before heirs receive it.

buildup.text: Estate tax applies to the total value of a deceased person's assets above a certain threshold.

discovery.text: In 2024, the U.S. exemption is about $13.6 million. Only estates above that pay the tax.

twist.text: Wealthy families use trusts, foundations, and gifting strategies to minimize estate taxes legally.

climax.text: Supporters call it a fairness tool. Critics call it a death tax that punishes success.

punchline.text: You can't take it with you—and the tax man knows it.

quiz.question: What does the estate tax apply to?
options: Assets of a deceased person above an exemption threshold
All income earned during a lifetime

details.summary: Estate and inheritance taxes are levied when wealth is transferred after death — estate tax is paid by the deceased's estate while inheritance tax is paid by the recipients. These taxes affect only the very wealthy due to high exemption thresholds.
details.whyItMatters: Estate taxes represent a fundamental policy choice about intergenerational wealth transfer and equality of opportunity, generating heated debate about fairness, family businesses, and concentrated wealth.
takeaways: Estate tax is paid by the estate before distribution; inheritance tax is paid by the person receiving the assets
The U.S. federal estate tax exemption is over $13 million per person, affecting less than 0.1% of estates
These taxes are designed to prevent extreme concentration of wealth across generations

faq.question: What is the difference between estate tax and inheritance tax?
faq.answer: Estate tax is paid by the deceased person's estate before assets are distributed to heirs. Inheritance tax is paid by the individual recipients on what they receive. The U.S. has a federal estate tax but no federal inheritance tax, though some states impose their own inheritance taxes.

faq.question: How much can you inherit tax-free?
faq.answer: In the U.S., the federal estate tax exemption is over $13 million per person (2024), meaning estates below that amount owe no federal estate tax. Married couples can effectively exempt over $26 million combined. This means fewer than 0.1% of all estates are subject to the federal estate tax.
